body:
Review pass 21. Correcting my own p0 fix suggestion before anyone implements it.

On bd-01KZXQAW39E8XCXJJVW7C7M2M6 I recommended replacing the dense frame hash with a hash of the sparse triplet @i/@p/@x/@Dim. I then validated that recommendation, and it is INCOMPLETE. Implemented naively it introduces a provenance correctness bug - two mathematically identical frames can get different signatures.

The failure case is a stored explicit zero. dgCMatrix keeps a sparsity PATTERN, and a stored entry whose value is 0 stays in @x unless dropped. Measured, with A0 holding one stored zero (199 stored entries) and B0 = drop0(A0) (198):

  identical(as.matrix(A0), as.matrix(B0))   TRUE    <- ground truth, same matrix
  dense signature equal                     TRUE    <- current behaviour, correct
  naive sparse-triplet signature equal      FALSE   <- my original suggestion, WRONG
  canonicalized sparse signature equal      TRUE    <- correct

CORRECTED FIX - canonicalize first:

  weights <- Matrix::drop0(as(as(frame$weights, "CsparseMatrix"), "generalMatrix"))
  ... weights = list(i = weights@i, p = weights@p, x = weights@x, dim = weights@Dim) ...

drop0 removes stored zeros; forcing CsparseMatrix + generalMatrix pins one representation so a symmetric or triangular subclass cannot hash differently from an equal general matrix.

Sensitivity is retained: a single entry perturbed by 1e-12 still gives a different signature. And the stability cases still hold - T->C round trip, double transpose, and no-op assignment all keep the signature; new nonzero and different dims still separate.

Whether a stored zero is reachable through the current .normalize_frame paths I did not establish, and it does not much matter: hashing a representation-dependent structure is fragile regardless, since a different construction route or a future Matrix release could introduce one. drop0 costs one call and removes the class of problem.

The p0 itself is unchanged - 18.6 GiB dense coercion at p=50000, canonicalized sparse hash still ~1657x smaller. Correction is on the bead.
